look_here_first: Look behind a blue-violet flower at the calyx: a thick white OR dark-violet FELT of short hairs covers it. A purple calyx can still be mealy blue sage. Compare broader, usually serrated stem leaves and condensed upright flower groups with azure sage's narrow nearly entire leaves and more open green-calyxed axis.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: not rosetted; only cauline opposite leaves

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's landscaping frame gives the upright flowering habit and repeated inflorescence architecture at field scale. Use that gestalt only as supporting context; the mealy/farinose calyx remains the decisive field character.

key_traits.label: Calyx
key_traits.text: UT Texas study: outer calyx densely white-haired or violet-haired, compressed side-to-side, about 5–8 mm long and ~10-ribbed. Not necessarily visibly white!

key_traits.label: Morphs
key_traits.text: White hairy form often blue flowers/white marks on lip; dark violet hairy form often darker blue without white marks. Both S. farinacea: do NOT use flower/calyx pigment as separate species.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite cauline leaves, blade often ~30–95 × 11–33 mm (occasional 5 mm narrow outliers), lanceolate/ovate, usually serrated; narrower S. azurea often ~4–8 mm wide and mostly entire.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Erect interrupted terminal panicle, condensed paired axillary cymes often 10+ flowers per cyme; many flowers crowded compared with azure sage.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Rhizomatous clonal perennial with several shoots, typically 30–100 cm in local descriptions; not rosetted.
